questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many courses in English and in postcolonial theory (decolonization – the Netherlands are very progressive in this field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UvA send mails in advance with information, otherwise I just asked other students for help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I just had to pay a fee, and then I got a offer later on. Just remember to check for mails often, you have to be quick to get a good location!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed it, definitely had an impact on making my exchange such a good experience! I felt very lucky with location and price. It wasn't far from my campus, so I could walk there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A bit confusing at first, understanding which courses I could take. I wasted a lot of time looking through the course catalogue.. You have to be quick at registration, otherwise you can get waitlisted and hope you'll get a spot later on (this happened to me).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed UvA with questions and got answers quite fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get many of my first choices. But most of my second choices. You can try to have courses at other faculties, which was really nice. I had 4/5 in humanities and 1 in social science, which I was really happy about, though - sadly - I was not able to get any in economics and business as I didn't have the prior knowledge.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to figure out early on, which courses are available to you. Perhaps email UvA for this information, if you can't find anything concerning this. And sit ready on time for registration, already knowing which courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my courses varied. They were very different, and the students had many different academic backgrounds, so for some it was easy, and for others it was all new. It really also depends a lot on the teacher's ambitions and their pace.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I mostly had seminars and here they valued and prioritized your reflections and oral skills/active participation in class a lot more than at my home university, where I almost only had traditional lectures and only one seminar. I also had multiple courses were they used alternative teaching methods such as students teaching the other students, which was really refreshing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aesthetics of Decolonization: Modern Art and Postcolonial Histories
Competing Heritages and Memories
Modern Art Globally Oriented
Teaching for Equality?: The Pedagogics of Feminist and Decolonial Education
Making Media: Production, Practices and Professions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Teaching for Equality?: The Pedagogics of Feminist and Decolonial Education!!! I never experienced a classroom to be such a welcoming and safe space, where you get acknowledged of bringing your whole person–your feelings, thoughts and what affects you in this moment of time. Tess is almost not a teacher, but more like a moderator, and the course was really enlightening in many aspects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is more expensive than what I assumed. More or less like Danish prices. Maybe a bit cheaper eating out, which I did a lot as my kitchen was so small.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike, which was cheap and almost never used public transportation. The city is quite small and it's easy to get around.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I used CREA, which is a cultural organisation offering creative courses to affordable prices for students. There's also one for sports, but I don't know the name. I also started a knitting club at my student housing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took a course called Visual Inventions at CREA. We painted the east tunnel in the Centraal Station, which was really fun and a nice way to meet new people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the sea, buy a museumskaart (then you can visit almost every museum in the NL as many times as you like), visit the markets and explore the city. Maybe do some day trips to nearby cities, but also cool to just chill in the city. Remember to relax and recharge.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the culture is really similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's hard to get local friends, so don't count on it. I actually mostly socialized with local students at the CREA course.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any... maybe that you don't really have to learn their language to get by? You can easily stay in the NL for a semester without learning much Dutch, which some people would find a pity.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone's so good at talking English, so language barrier is not really a problem. I really appreciated how openminded and easygoing people in Amsterdam are like, sometimes they sing openly on the street, they never use curtains even though they have enormous windows facing right to the canals and they also want to help you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the extra free time and explore the city's many offers, especially the arts and cultures, but remember to do things in your own pace and find time to relax too. It's okay not to socialize all the time. Also, remember you don't need to be perfect, instead be brave, try new things and practice whatever you can get better at – this is such a nice opportunity to do so.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask another exchange students if you have any doubts or troubles. Everyone is more or less in the same situation as you and can relate and probably also help you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Practicing my oral skills and feeling an improvement – it gradually gets easier. Of course, also meeting new people and nourishing new friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Working with my performance anxiety and having a traumatic experience with one teacher. But I found a good way to get on top of it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
